trust_decision.summary: Which caller-supplied keys the shared assign() helper copies onto a fresh attributes/converter object; at the pinned commit it copies every for-in key, including an own '__proto__' key from JSON.parse, which swaps the per-instance prototype so the set() serialisation loop emits attacker-chosen inherited attributes.

landing_point.why: The summary names assign(); it is a 9-line file and the only merge helper in the repo.

fix_sites.entry_point: Cookies.set / Cookies.remove / Cookies.withAttributes / Cookies.withConverter (public API, all call assign)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No real route to dismiss: all four public calls go through the one assign() at src/api.mjs:10,84,90,93, so the one-line guard covers them all.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: assign merges defaults with overrides, including an explicit undefined that removes a default (withAttributes({path: undefined})) and remove() adding expires:-1. The set() for-in loop must still serialise the merged keys. A null-prototype target, or keeping '__proto__' as an own key, makes the loop emit or .split() a non-string '__proto__' attribute.

O6_input_shapes: own '__proto__' key from JSON.parse in the attributes argument of set()
same key in the attributes of remove() / withAttributes()
same key in the converter of withConverter()

O8b_injection_room.sibling: get() builds jar from document.cookie names with plain-object keys; a planted parsed-cookie-to-object merge helper could copy a '__proto__' cookie name onto the jar
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The read side already indexes a plain {} by attacker-influenced cookie names. A maintainer adding a 'getAll as object' or JSON-cookie helper would plausibly reuse a naive merge.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a separate converter-merge (or a deep merge for nested converter options) that does not reuse assign()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Converters are objects of functions; a second merge written for them would be a believable second implementation, but it is only a WHERE-type sibling in the same file.

O9_family: prototype pollution (per-instance prototype hijack) leading to cookie-attribute injection, CWE-1321

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=20, npm, rollup, grunt, QUnit via grunt-contrib-qunit with headless Chrome (puppeteer)
services: local grunt-contrib-connect static server on 127.0.0.1:9998 for browser tests
O10_build.project_tests: test/tests.js 'write' and 'setup' modules (withAttributes/withConverter at test/tests.js:3-80, attribute writes at test/tests.js:246-447) run in headless Chrome; test/node.js only checks noop calls without document.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Use Object.create(null) as the assign target or filter only in set(); the first keeps '__proto__' as an own key that the set() loop then serialises or crashes on.

out_of_scope_notes: get() uses a plain {} jar with `found in jar` (src/api.mjs:57-64), so cookies named like Object.prototype members (toString, constructor) are skipped or shadowed; this is a separate correctness issue, not attribute injection.
The set() for-in loop (src/api.mjs:24) also emits enumerable properties from a globally polluted Object.prototype; global pollution is outside this per-instance advisory.
